newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ASTRA has stake in owner of oil spill ship.
newsitem.headline: ASTRA has stake in owner of oil spill ship.

text.p: Argentine oil firm ASTRA said Friday it has an indirect 35 percent stake in the company that operates a ship that caused an oil slick off the Uruguayan coast.

"That ship (the Panamanian registered San Jorge) is owned by Oilsud Corporation, controlled by Transportes Maritimos Petroleros SA, the latter being the operator of the ship," ASTRA's President Jose Ranero Diaz told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange in a letter.
"Astra has an indirect 35 percent stake in Transportes Maritimos Petroleros SA through Antares Naviera SA and Inasa (Inversora Naviera Argentina SA)," he added.
Spain's Repsol has a controlling 47.5 percent stake in Astra.

The San Jorge, loaded with 58,000 tonnes of crude, ran aground Saturday 20 miles (32 km) off the Uruguayan coast spilling 200 tonnes of oil in the sea. It was on its way from the southern Argentine port of Comodoro Rivadavia to San Sebastian, in Brazil.

Ranero Diaz said the ship and Transportes Maritimos Petroleros have an "adecuate insurance coverage against the hull, machinery, freight losses, environmental pollution and other damage with top international insurance companies."
